reviews.comment: Interesting subject and good lecturer, but a bit condescending. Also, this course does venture much into the 20th century and is more focused on early American constitutional history.

Brooks is a cool professor if you see him in office hours however, his lectures are hard to get through. He knows just about everything about history and expects you to. He expects you you read a lot and remember the details. Only 3 grades for the semester (2 exam tests in class and a 8 page paper). 2 absences allowed.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Brooks is not your typical history prof. He engages the class through his stories and insights. He has a historical sense of humor which gives him character. HIs tests are literally his lectures so type as much as you can and just reread your notes. People that don't do well are the ones who are on different laptop tabs. Pay attention- easy A.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Brooks lectures are like story times! Legit if you don't want to fall asleep, take Brooks. Go to class, take notes, and you'll pass. I never touch the books and got a B just by re visiting my notes. He is the best storyteller by far!
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Attendance isn't required but 80% of the tests are based on lecture. I normally hate history I found his class to be quite enjoyable. He focuses mainly on the political aspects but he tells it more like a story and that makes it a lot easier to actually retain the info. I didn't study or actually read but got a B without trying. Taken in the summer
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: 3 tests 1 essay (you have the choice between 3 topics to write about). Each topic is due at a different time throughout the semester, so choose wisely. He is very caring and really wants you to do good so office hours can be helpful. Very lecture heavy, but he tells history like a story so it is easy to follow and he keeps it interesting.
reviews.ratingTags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Brooks was one of my favorite teachers this semester. Some lectures may seem long but he DEFINITELY makes the subject interesting. If you have 2 or less absences in the class, he will boost you up a letter grade if you're within 2 or 3 points. After 3 tests and 1 paper, I had a grade of an 87. Since I had perfect attendance, I had an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: brooks was the best professor I've had so far this spring semester. his tests are from his lectures. he keeps his students engaged and answers any questions you may have. theres only 3 exams and one paper. if you do bad on the paper or exam, he lets you do another paper to replace your lowest grade. I LOVED HIM!
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Charle's a really cool and fun professor. He is always interesting and easy to follow and take notes on. He emails a lesson plan out before every lecture. You have to write an essay but can choose 1 of 3 to do. Perfect attendance bumps your grade up and poor attendance lowers letter grades. Tests aren't bad but definitely study lecture notes.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Inspirational--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Lectures can feel a bit long, but they can also be interesting.. He tries to make them enjoyable and even if they aren't, they cover most of what you need to know for tests. He has a pretty straight forward attendance policy.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Brooks gives the best lectures. Make sure to take good notes or record them (he will let you if you ask.) He emails out lecture outlines, but that is it. Tests are very much based on the lectures - if you take good notes you will be fine. Its probably a good idea to leave your phone/laptop in your bag for this one. You need your full attention.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Doesn't use Ecampus because he is stuck in the past. Doesn't have any information outside the lecture besides a tiny bad outline he sends out in email right before class. Lecture isn't worth going to, and much of what he lectures is inconsistent with the textbook. Entire class is a  boring lecture, and some of it is wrong. Do not take this class.

Great lecturer! Attendance can be considered mandatory from my pov b/c if you have solid attendance, he gives 5 extra points on the final and bumps you up a grade if you're at most 2 points from the next letter grade. Put in a small amount of effort and you'll earn at least a B. Asks many questions to get the class involved. Would recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great guy. While attendance was mandatory for a grade, the class was interesting, and Brooks is an amazing lecturer

Mr. Brooks lectures every class, He sends out a lecture outline for each class and gives three tests and one paper. Each test is based off of all of the lectures that were prior to it. Easy to understand and is willing to help or let you record lectures if you ask.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: RECORD THE LECTURES. After I started doing that I was able to take better notes. He doesn't give slides, just outlines. His tests are a bit hard, but if you understand the material you should pass them. There was one paper and I got an A, (others didn't do as well). You can ask for clarification and help. Key Terms from the textbook are important!
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you're more than 30 minutes late to class more than twice you drop a full letter grade. Make sure you take the best notes you can as that's all you have to study for the tests. The tests aren't super easy but not too hard either. I managed to get an A on the last essay you could do without reading the book. Easy B, but a hard A.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Brooks is a great lecturer- he makes the topics interesting to listen to. He has no visuals in class,  though he sends outlines via email each week. There are three tests and a paper. Take good notes and study well for the test and you will pass! Your seating is assigned so pick a good seat by the second day. He picks vocabulary from the textbook.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very good prof. If you're not an auditory learner I would not recommend him. He has no presentation slides, just lectures. All the information is in his head. Funny, smart man. Make sure to read all the assigned books, and you get to choose which paper to write on the books. Don't undermine the tests, they are more difficult than you'd assume.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He a very nice professor but his lectures are boring. I found myself toning out by accident and missing important things. The tests are very difficult.  It was 30 MC and 20 T/F questions. I went over my notes and barely managed to pass the tests. I had to q drop because that class would have ruined my GPA. Attendance is taken everyday.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I did not appreciate his lectures that much. He seemed to jump back and forth with small details while lecturing instead of being straightforward. His tests were not that simple either. If this is your first semester in college or history is not your strong subject, I would suggest finding an easier professor.  Overall, he is a good professor.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: 3 tests, 1 paper. That's what your grade revolves around. Had to drop the class. Will never take him again and would not recommend to ANYBODY.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Brooks is amazing.  I was worried at the beginning of the year because he only takes four grades the whole semester, and almost all questions on his tests come from his lectures, but he is great.  Lectures were interesting and entertaining.  He genuinely cares about his students and is still one of my favorite professors.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: His lectures are boring but he is clear with the info. The tests are solely composed of everything he talks about in class so take good notes and you will do well on the tests. There are only four 3 tests and 1 essay each worth 25% so you need to do well. They are an easy B but a hard A. Attendance is ABSOLUTELY mandatory or he will drop your grade
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Charles Brooks is an amazing professor.  He lectures History with ease and never looks at the textbook.  You will be emailed a lecture outline every day before class and he lectures directly based on the outline.   There are only 4 grades the entire semester: 3 exams and an essay. He is very giving and gives out extra credit and hints a lot.
reviews.ratingTags: Hilarious--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: sweetheart, passionate about history, provides outline for lecture, tough when grading papers, average level difficulty tests.  warning: if you miss more than three classes, he drops you a letter grade, but if you attend all lectures except three he adds points to your final and will bump you from an 88 to a 90 or 78 to 80
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: This prof was very nice. I took this class over the summer so it was every day. He does not use a textbook and exams are strictly based on lectures. The exams are not hard, but you have to listen to everything he says in class to do well. I was sitting at a high B and he let me write an extra credit paper for an A. Loved this prof!
reviews.ratingTags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took him in an upper level class and he doesn't let you forget that. He gave no outlines or reviews for the test and there were only 3 grades in the class which meant you had to do well on all of them. If you pay attention and read, you should do well but just make sure you go deeper than just the info he presents in the lectures.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I HATED HISTORY before this class. The lectures are great! He sure keeps your attention, and as long as you show up and listen to what he has to say, you will pass for sure. Definitely recommend him!
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved this class. Kept the lectures interesting and very organized. He gives an outline each lecture and all you have to do is take notes and learn the key terms and you will do fine. One of my best profs last year!
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: This is a very straightforward class. Four grades: one essay over a book, three in-class exams. The exams are not too hard. What he lectures is what will be on the test. I dont even like history, but never found myself bored in class. He is honestly one of the best lecture professor Ive had at A&M.

If you find early U.S. History to be an interesting topic then you DEFINITELY need to take this class! there's only one paper due per semester with 3 non-cumulative tests. read the textbook chapters, read the cliff notes on the two books that you don't write your essay on, AND GO TO CLASS AND PAY ATTENTION. best history class ever.

Professor Brooks obviously enjoys history and shows this through is lectures. Some lectures felt a little long but overall Brooks kept the lectures clear and semi-interesting. Brooks wants you to do well and if you show up to class (except two days) he'll give you points. Only 3 semi-easy tests and one paper that isn't grader too hard. Take him.

If I would have studied diligently and kept up with readings, I might have gotten an A. There are 4 tests including the final which is not cumulative with one paper to choose out of three options. The papers are over books that you have to read anyway. I would take again, but just stay on top of things. If you miss more than two classes, you fail.

long lectures with no visual aid. 3 assigned books to read and an essay over one of them. 3 test, must take notes and listen. can make an A if you put in the effort. Not the best hist prof but definitely not the worst.

You must attend class. The lectures are quite long and boring and all he does is talk. If you are a visual learner don't take him. You also need to have the willpower to focus and listen. Its history so its not too bad but he has his own specific things needed to know for the tests. 3 tests, 30 multiple choice questions 20 true/false & 1 essay
Really good lecturer, if you show up to class and pay attention it will be hard to not get an A. He does require one paper over your choice of three books,  but its not a big deal.

Lectures are somewhat interesting and I am not a history person. Take notes over everything he says and study the key terms in the textbook and you'll do just fine on the tests. The 1 essay is graded a little tough but nothing you can't conquer. If you have more than 2 unexcused absences then your grade is dropped a letter.

The first exam I studied very hard for and thought I did well and did not. The test format was not clear as to what the questions were really asking. Interesting class but he is too difficult of a grader.
He's amazing as well as being incredibly engaging. First time I've loved learning about history!

LOVED his class. Has review sessions for all the tests which are very helpful. No homework. 3 tests, 1 paper. Takes attendance everyday, but you should come because his tests are mostly based off lecture, and his lectures are funny and interesting. If you attend all the lectures you get extra credit. He's fair, kind, & makes lectures interesting.

Dr. Brooks is amazing. He really loves U.S. history and is a really good professor. Attendence is mandatory but he gives some credit always showing up. Makes the lectures interesting and always wants to start student discussions. The book is only needed for key terms. Test are all multiple choice. Easy A if you put the effort.
Lectures were really boring, and the TA did all of the grading. He said the textbook was mandatory but we never used it, and the test questions were worded crazy. Attendance is mandatory

have to go to class, attendance policy drops your letter grade after you miss 2 classes, if you don't miss more than 2 he gives 3 bonus points on final.  Lectures are long but interesting, one essay that is graded pretty fairly and 3 tests that aren't too hard, very funny

Dr. Brooks is an awesome professor, lectures are a bit long, doesn't use any visual aid just talks the whole time but makes it interesting. 2 tests plus the final (not cumulative) assigns a paper but is very clear cut on what he wants, attendance is a must you drop a letter grade if you don't go. Overall great professor, would definitely take again

Dr. Brooks is awesome. His lectures can be a little long, but they make up 70% of the test material so go to class. He takes attendance, but you're rewarded for showing up to class at the end of the semester. Theres an essay, but you get to pick which reading you would like to do it over, so thats nice. Pretty funny guy, would take his class again.

Lecture based exams with very little percentage of textbook. Must read three novels from those you pick the one to write an essay about.  Brooks shows true passion for history. He is a funny man. Lectures can get pretty long, but they're interesting. Take notes quickly for he moves on fast. I highly recommend him. He takes attendance.
Tests are 70% lecture material. Must go to class, but they are interesting. Brooks makes history interesting.  Must take notes quickly-he talks quickly Great man

Tests are 70% based on lectures, but the lectures are pretty entertaining and easy to understand. Attendance is mandatory, if you have more than 2 unexcused absences he drops your grade some and if you have 2 unexcused absences or less he gives you extra points on your overall grade. Tests are average difficulty

One of my favorite professors at A&M. Attendance is part of your grade, so you have to go to class. He tells you up front that the exams are 70% lecture, 30% textbook. You only have to write 1 essay for the class and you have 3 book options to write it over. He doesn't use any powerpoints, just lectures. He's a brilliant professor. Loved his class

Excellent teacher, knew the content extremely well and lectured it very effectively and efficiently. Always kept the class intrigued. Knew the content amazingly well. His tests did happen to be pretty challenging though. Great guy and very personal, kept the class entertained and had a good sense of humor.

Overall Brooks was a good prof. Tests are straight from lectures, 50 questions, 30 multiple choice & 20 T/F. He takes attendance and if you miss more than 2 classes you drop a letter grade. Lectures were good and he kept me interested in what he was saying.

Very long lectures and the tests are a bit little hard, but overall ok. He does sometimes make time for review sessions so you have to take advantage of that. Only 3 tests and 1 essay that you can choose from 3 readings

Dr. Brooks doesn't use a powerpoint which worried me at first but he is great at making class like on big story! He keeps it interesting and is super passionate about what he does which everyone respects. He will help you if you need it willingly!
The tests are worded weird. It is more of application than memorizing dates. You don't have to read the book, just make sure to do the vocabulary in the book.

Brooks is so amazing. His lectures are so well structured and he's very passionate about the subject and wants his students to succeed. Follow the outlines he sends out and use those to study!!!  Attendance is mandatory. At the end of the semester I ended with a 88 but because I only missed 2 classes I was able to argue my case and he gave me an A!

tests are 70% lecture based, 30% vocal from the books. he is very interested in history but his lectures can get very boring. Tests are 30 MC, 20 TF. never made above a 75 on his tests. one paper which is graded pretty fairly (I got an 85 and did it the night before). He emails an outline to the lecture the night before, USE IT

I was not interested in History before his class, I was concerned that I would not do well in the class because he doesn't use powerpoints but I was wrong! He makes the class interesting and he is passionate about it which makes him that much better! I recommend this class!

Dr. Brooks class is not that hard but you do have to go to class. He takes attendance and if you miss more than 2 classes you drop a letter grade. He has 3 tests (not cumulative) and then a paper reading assignment. His tests are mostly based on lectures and gives a lecture outline to help you get the important points. Overall good professor!
For someone who didn't like history before, I really enjoyed him as a professor. He is really funny and is really passionate about what he is teaching.
Easy A - bring laptop to type notes; his lectures are very interesting and "stick" because of that. Hard to imagine anyone not liking him he was great.

Dr. Brooks is really intrigued with history and  will help you out if you need it. Three tests, non-cumulative and one paper. Usually the book is only used for key terms but he my refer to a few pages that you should look over. If he gives a review session himself, GO TO IT. Long lectures but he provides useful outlines prior to class to print off.
Dr. Brooks is truly interested in History. He tells funny, related stories to the topics in order to keep you interested.

He gave lectures that were long and sometimes seemed to drag on forever, however the tests were always over what he talks about. There are three tests and one paper. I studied a decent amount and got a B on most things. Reading the book may help, although if you just pay attention in class you will pick up on most topics.

I love Charles Brooks!! He does not have any powerpoints and only lectures, but his lectures are very interesting! You have to go to class. His tests are mainly over his lectures, and they are multiple choice and TF. Only part of textbook you need to look at is the key terms. Overall I would love to take him again, he is very willing to help you!
He's awesome. Very passionate about his material so it keeps you interested.  The test aren't too bad, completely over the lectures and some vocab, they are multiple choice with some true false.

Great Professor! Very knowledgeable on the subject and loves to share cool stories with the class. His lecture is like one big interesting story. Keeps you interested instead of falling asleep and helps with remembering the material for tests. Tests are from lectures and vocab from the textbook. Great professor and class overall!

AWESOME PROFESSOR!! The lectures are honestly so interesting that I don't even pay attention to the time... when it's time to go I don't want to leave!! No powerpoints or any confusing stuff, just lecture and discussion! love the class!

An excellent professor. He makes his lecture very interesting. His tests are not that difficult if you pay attention in class and he grades them fairly. I definitely recommend to take him for Hist 105.

He's an awesome teacher! I loved this class. He makes his lectures interesting and funny. He talks fast, so taking notes on a laptop is easiest. He has three tests--not cumulative and one paper from an additional reading. The tests are based mainly from the lectures, but there are questions from the reading, too. I definitely recommend this course!

I thought his tests were hard. He had 5 options that were all right and you had to choose which one he thought was the best. Attendance is mandatory. He has 2 exams and a paper, as well as a final exam. The paper is what brought my average up. He is a very interesting professor, but I thought he was challenging.

I had never been interested in knowing history until this class. He tells things like a story, with occasional stories that can spark interest as well. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you go to class he will give extra points. All you have is 3 tests (no cumulative final) and one essay of your choice over a reading. I overall enjoyed this class!
He pretty cool guy. Kinda slow talker so you can take notes pretty well
Pay attention and take notes, and read the book. His first and last test include MC TF and essay's, and the two middle tests are all MC and TF. Those are the only grades given.
INCREDIBLY BORING...LECTURES ENTIRE CLASS PERIOD AND DOES NOT LINE UP WITH BOOK
capricious grader. watch out!
No Comments
